D45b-001.title: ASN.1 encoding mismatch - KDCREQ/KDCREQBody missing all context-specific tags
D45b-001.description: The Go structs for KDCREQ and KDCREQBody lack explicit context-specific tags required by RFC 4120. All fields are encoded with universal tags instead of the required explicit context-specific tags [1], [2], [3], [4] for KDCREQ and [0] through [8] for KDCREQBody.
D45b-001.evidence: Samba4 KDC returns EOF / silently rejects Aether-generated AS-REQ

D45b-002.title: PAData missing context-specific tags [1] and [2]
D45b-002.description: The PAData struct fields PADataType and PADataValue lack explicit tags [1] and [2] respectively. They are encoded as universal INTEGER and OCTET STRING instead of context-specific [1] and [2].

D45b-003.title: PrincipalName missing context-specific tags [0] and [1] when embedded
D45b-003.description: The PrincipalName struct has a custom MarshalASN1/UnmarshalASN1 using principalNameASN1 with correct tags, but when embedded in KDCREQBody, the custom marshaler is not invoked because Go's encoding/asn1 uses the struct field directly, not the custom marshaler for non-pointer embedded structs.
D45b-003.expected_tags: name-type [0] Int32, name-string [1] SEQUENCE OF KerberosString

D45b-004.title: Realm requires GeneralString encoding (tag 27)
D45b-004.description: The Realm type is defined as 'type Realm string' which encoding/asn1 encodes as IA5String (tag 22) or PrintableString (tag 19). Kerberos requires GeneralString (tag 27) per RFC 4120.

root_cause: Missing explicit context-specific tags in ASN.1 struct definitions. Go's encoding/asn1 does not automatically apply context-specific tags from ASN.1 module definitions - they must be explicitly specified in struct tags using 'explicit,tag:N'.
workaround_noted: keytab auth works (kinit -k -t keytab), proving ccache, crypto, TGS, and downstream operations are correct. Defect is isolated to AS-REQ construction.
diagnostic_commands: kinit -V user1@AETHER.TEST (WORKS - proves KDC is healthy)
KRB5_TRACE=/dev/stderr kinit -V user1@AETHER.TEST (shows correct AS-REQ from MIT)
